problem: splitUsage splits on "\n" only (:103) and matches each line against USAGE_LINE, whose `.` does not match a trailing "\r". The regex it replaced used `[^\n]*`, which took the \r. A raw result with CRLF line endings (a reviewer or host that writes raw/<reviewer>.txt on Windows) ends in `KERYX_USAGE {...}\r`: the line does not match, it stays in the body, and it counts as reply text, so `trailing` turns false for every usage line above it.
impact: Every dispatch whose raw file is CRLF reads as `unknown` usage and leaves its usage line in the body (a KERYX_USAGE line makes an empty reply non-empty, so isEmptyRecord is false for a CRLF placeholder + usage file). The round's token total undercounts by the number of such dispatches. No gate reads usage, so the cost is a wrong spend line in report.md, plus a CRLF placeholder file escaping the empty-reply handling in the ledger.
suggested_fix: Strip a trailing \r from each line before matching (`line.replace(/\r$/, "")`), or make the pattern `(.*?)\r?$`; add a CRLF case to the dispatch-usage tests.
evidence: dispatch-usage.ts:53 `(.*)$` without the s flag; :103 `raw.split("\n")`; :109-112 non-matching lines set trailing=false. Prior pattern in the r2 diff: `[ \t]+([^\n]*)$` with the m flag.

problem: flowPackageDirs reads and JSON-parses the manifest of every standalone package under .metaproject/reviews for each flow asked about. collectFlowGovernance (src/governance/aggregate.ts:44-49) calls readFlowReviewManifests once per flow dir, serially, so `keryx governance report` does flows x packages manifest reads; loop.ts:488 and flow/review-gate.ts:462 do the same per flow they inspect.
impact: At this repository's size (434 flows, 31 standalone packages) that is about 13,500 small sequential reads per governance report; it grows with both counts (1,000 flows x 300 committed packages is 300,000 reads, tens of seconds on a single-threaded CLI). Correct, only slow.
suggested_fix: Read the standalone packages' manifest heads once per call chain and group by bound flow (a Map flowDir -> package dirs), or pass a pre-read head list into readFlowReviewManifests; read the heads with a bounded Promise.all.
evidence: package-location.ts:61-76 (loop over reviewsRoot with readManifestHead per entry, per flow); governance/aggregate.ts:44-49 (per-flow call); governance/spend.ts:23.

problem: saveDispatchRecord is a read-modify-write on save_result_to (readFile at :345, writeFile at :315) with no serialisation. Two spawn_subagent calls in one turn that name the same save_result_to (the parallel dispatch of a slice and its retry, or the timed-out child's save running while the parent re-dispatches the same slice) both read the same prior state and the last write wins.
impact: One dispatch's KERYX_USAGE / KERYX_USAGE_OTHER line (or its result) is overwritten, so the round's spend undercounts by that dispatch; with a complete result in the file, a later non-final record can rewrite the file from a stale read and drop the other's `kept` usage. Needs two children writing the same path in one turn; the review driver gives each (reviewer, wave) its own path, so only a hand dispatch reaches it.
suggested_fix: Serialise saves per absolute path with a small in-process promise chain keyed by abs (Map<string, Promise>), or write via a temp file and rename after re-reading under that chain.
evidence: spawn-subagent-tool.ts:344-363 (read at :345, write via writeRecordFile :311-320); callers :1948-1949, :2303, :2343, :2368, :2407.

problem: saveDispatchRecord treats any non-empty earlier record as a complete result. A timed-out or stopped dispatch is saved non-final (:2303, :2407) and, over an empty path, becomes the file's reply. A later re-dispatch that also ends non-final (times out after writing its whole REVIEW_RESULT) then takes the kept branch: its text is discarded entirely (round 2 still kept it in <target>.partial), only its usage is added, and the parent is told 'the complete result an earlier dispatch saved ... was kept'. The earlier record's own usage line carries partial:true for a timeout, but the check does not read it.
impact: The ledger and retry-eval read the first, shorter partial while the retry's fuller result is lost from disk; the tool note misreports it as complete. The parent only has a bounded summary of the retry's text.
suggested_fix: Keep the earlier file only when it is a final record (its trailing KERYX_USAGE is not partial, or record finality explicitly in the file); otherwise let a non-final record with text replace a non-final one, or keep the newer partial beside it.
evidence: src/harness/tool/builtin/spawn-subagent-tool.ts:2303 saveRecord(partial, {final:false, partial:true}); :348-355 kept branch writes prior.body and drops record.text; recordSaveNote :369 'the complete result ... was kept'; the delta removed the `<target>.partial` write of saveTimedOutPartial

quote: } else if (ch === ";" || ch === "&" || ch === "|" || ch === "\n") endCommand();
problem: shellCommands ends a command at every unquoted `&`, including the one in the redirection `2>&1` (and `>&2`). `keryx review start --pr 7975 2>&1` is therefore read as two commands (`... 2>` and `1`), so keryxReviewInvocations sets alone=false (:200) and the tracker ignores keryx's `# managed review:` / `path:` output (:295). For `cd sub && keryx review start --pr N 2>&1`, sub is never added to roots, because roots come only from paths (:320-322), not from invocation.cwd.
impact: In the subdirectory layout flow 460 targets, a session that redirects stderr (common for agents) never scans sub: the gate nudges with NO_PACKAGE_BLOCKER while the package is open, and after `keryx review complete <id>` the closed package under sub is still never seen, so the nudge continues until the stall/continue cap.
suggested_fix: Treat `&` as a separator only when it is not part of a redirection (preceded by `>`/`<` or followed by `>`), and/or add invocation.cwd as a root whenever an executed `keryx review` command ran in a directory other than cwd.
evidence: src/review/completion-gate.ts:165 (split), :200 (alone), :295 (pendingCalls only when alone), :320-322 (roots only via namePaths); test :348-360 covers only `;`/`&&` compounds

quote: if (widest === undefined || result.changedLines > widest.changedLines || result.files.length > widest.files.length) widest = result;
problem: The 'wider of recorded and default base' rule replaces the measured diff when EITHER dimension is larger, so it can keep a diff that is smaller in the other. Recorded base: 10 files, 900 changed lines; default base: 11 files, 100 lines -> the default one is kept, and autoDepth reads 100 changed lines.
impact: The light recheck can under-measure changed lines (or files) and accept a light dispatch that the recorded base alone would have refused, which is what the widening was added to prevent.
suggested_fix: Take the per-dimension maximum (files and changedLines separately), or compare one size measure consistently.
evidence: src/review/coverage.ts:586-592 diffOfTarget loop; resolveDiffBases :568-576 and the packageDiffStats doc say the wider of the two is measured

problem: saveDispatchRecord (new in this delta) replaced saveTimedOutPartial's `.partial` diversion. Now a non-final record (a timeout or a stopped child with text) that finds any non-empty record at save_result_to keeps the existing body and writes nothing else of the new text. It does not check whether the existing record is final. If an earlier dispatch's PARTIAL text is there (written non-final, its usage marked `partial: true`), a retry's partial text is thrown away completely. recordSaveNote (line 369) then tells the parent that 'the complete result an earlier dispatch saved ... was kept', which is false.
impact: Trigger: dispatch 1 of a reviewer times out after writing some text, so raw/<r>-w<n>.txt holds partial A. The parent re-dispatches to the same driver result path, and dispatch 2 also times out or stops, possibly after emitting its whole REVIEW_RESULT block. Outcome: B is written nowhere, the ledger parses A, and the parent is told a complete result is on disk. At 375279e78, B went to `<path>.partial`. No reader picked that file up, but it kept the text on disk for the operator. Now the text is gone.
suggested_fix: Divert only for an earlier FINAL record. Record finality in the file (for example, the `partial: true` usage flag, or an explicit marker for non-final saves). Let a non-final record replace an earlier non-final one, or keep it beside the earlier one as `<path>.partial`. Word the note from what was actually there. Add a test: a timeout with text A, then a timeout with text B to the same path, leaves B readable and does not claim a complete result.
evidence: spawn-subagent-tool.ts:348 condition, which tests only !record.final and !isEmptyRecord(existing). spawn-subagent-tool.ts:2303 saves a timeout as `saveRecord(partial, { final: false, partial: true })`, and :2407 saves a non-Completed status as final=false. spawn-subagent-tool.ts:369 note text. At 375279e78 (git show), saveTimedOutPartial wrote to `${abs}.partial` when the target was non-blank. harness-robustness.test.ts row 14 tests partial-over-complete and empty-over-anything, but not partial-over-partial.

class_scope.enumeration_method: Every caller of saveRecord in spawn-subagent-tool.ts: timeout (:2303), rate-limited (:2350 area, empty text only), empty reply (:2368, empty text only), and completion (:2407, non-final when status is not Completed). Only the timeout and the non-Completed-with-text paths carry text into the kept branch.

quote: } else if (ch === ";" || ch === "&" || ch === "|" || ch === "\n") endCommand();
problem: The new shell reader splits a command at every unquoted `&`, including the one in the redirection `2>&1` (and `&>`). So `keryx review start --pr 7 2>&1` reads as two commands: `keryx review start --pr 7 2>` and `1`. keryxReviewInvocations counts the `1` as another command, so `alone` is false (line 200). The tracker then never trusts the `# managed review:` / `path:` lines that start, attach or ingest printed. This defeats the LG-002 fix for its own case: with `cd sub && keryx review start --pr 7 2>&1`, the root `sub` is never learned from the reply.
impact: Trigger: a session runs `cd sub && keryx review start --pr <n> 2>&1`. Appending `2>&1` is routine for agents. Later commands name the package only by id (`cd sub && keryx review complete <id> 2>&1`). Outcome: findReviewGateState scans only cwd and never sees the open or closed package under sub. The gate keeps nudging with NO_PACKAGE_BLOCKER until the stall limit, both while the review runs and after it closes. In the plain cwd case the open package is still found by mtime, so the effect is limited to subdirectory packages and to packages from earlier sessions that are named only through output.
suggested_fix: In shellCommands, treat an `&` directly after `>` or `<`, or directly before `>`, as part of a redirection and not a separator. Drop redirection words from `args`, or at least do not let them count as other commands. Add a test: `cd sub && keryx review start --pr 7975 2>&1` with the same reply names sub's package.
evidence: completion-gate.ts:165 splits on `&`. completion-gate.ts:200 `const alone = found.length === 1 && others === 0`. The tracker queues pendingCalls only when `invocation.alone && OPENING_SUBCOMMANDS.has(...)`, and a call that is not pending has its output lines skipped. completion-gate.test.ts covers `cd sub && keryx review start --pr 7975` (no redirect) and compound lines with `;`/`&&`, but not `2>&1`.

class_scope.enumeration_method: shellCommands is the only tokenizer. keryxReviewInvocations is its only caller and feeds both `alone` and `args`, so this is the one site.

quote: quote only — as an exact substring of exactly one line, then it stops — nothing
problem: This delta added MIN_SUBSTRING_QUOTE_CHARS = 12 (locate.ts:131). A one-line quote shorter than 12 characters that is not a whole line is now `unlocatable` (kind absent), even when exactly one line contains it. Neither the CLI reference nor the quote descriptions in the schemas that reviewers are handed mention the floor. All of them still say a one-line quote is placed as an exact substring of exactly one line.
impact: Trigger: a reviewer follows the schema and quotes a distinctive fragment under 12 characters, such as an identifier. Outcome: ingest flags the finding quote_unlocated with line null, readiness item quotes-located fails, and the round needs a re-quote or a waiver. The documents promised that such a quote would be placed.
suggested_fix: Add 'of at least 12 characters (MIN_SUBSTRING_QUOTE_CHARS); a shorter fragment must be a whole line' to the substring pass in all four places, and keep the copies identical.
evidence: locate.ts:131 and :248-250 (the floor and its reason). docs/docs/cli-reference.md:6679-6680. The quote description at src/gdskills/bundled/skills/review/review-orchestrator/reviewer-finding.schema.json:85, the same at .metaproject/skills/gdskills/review/review-orchestrator/reviewer-finding.schema.json:85, and src/gdskills/contracts/review-finding.schema.json:195. A grep for 'too short|MIN_SUBSTRING|12 char' over the docs, the schemas and the delta-docs.diff finds no mention.

class_scope.enumeration_method: grep 'as an exact substring of exactly one line' over docs, src/gdskills and .metaproject/skills: these four statements of the matcher order are every hit.

quote: if (manifest !== undefined) for (const reviewer of fixSliceRoles(manifest)) names.add(reviewer);
problem: Before this change, packageReviewers added every role a slice was routed to (`for (const entry of manifest.slices) for (const role of entry.roles ?? []) names.add(role)`). It now adds only the required set plus the roles of fix and second-look slices. review plan rewrites the drivers from this set (review-plan.ts writeWaveDrivers) and removes the stale ones. In a light round, requiredReviewers keeps only logic, testing and one conventions reviewer (coverage.ts:397-405), and light qualification is path-only: at most 5 files and 300 lines, outside RISK_PATH_GATES (coverage.ts:106, :146). So slice routing still tags a new slice that spawns a process or builds a git argv for review-security-code (slice-routing.ts:116-117, SECURITY_PRINCIPLE), but that role gets no driver, `review next` never lists it, and no gate notices. The delta kept this union for fix slices only (fixSliceRoster), so the 458 M3 guarantee now holds for fix lines and not for new lines in a light round.
attack_vector: A PR author keeps the change within the light limits (<=5 files, <=300 changed lines, no core/flow/layout path) and adds `Bun.spawn(["sh","-c", input])` in an ordinary src file. Under `--depth auto` the round is light. Routing marks the slice for review-security-code, but `review slice --package` and `review plan` write no security driver. The round then completes READY without the security reviewer ever reading the injected command line. Before this delta, the driver for that role was written.
impact: Security review of process, argv, git and input-derived path code in small PRs now depends on the logic reviewer alone. The routing summary still reports review-security-code for the slice, so the manifest says the code was routed to security review when it was never dispatched.
suggested_fix: Count a SECURITY_PRINCIPLE / process-spawn content hit in the light-round risk class, so such a diff is full depth. Or keep the content-routed security role in both the estimate (roleDispatchWaves callers) and the drivers. Either way plan.json and the drivers still agree, and the content rule is not silently dropped.
evidence: git log -L packageReviewers (ddd2a91d7) shows the deleted `manifest.slices ... entry.roles` loop; src/review/wave-drivers.ts:21-36 at HEAD; src/review/coverage.ts:21-25,397-405 (light set and limits), :106-108,:146 (path-only risk class); src/review/slice-routing.ts:116-117 (content rules that pick review-security-code); src/commands/review-plan.ts:291 (plan rewrites drivers from packageReviewers).
